correctness.rationale: All nine pairwise mixed indicators are derived by symmetric fair sign enumeration, conditioning and probability-integral-transform integration. Summing the explicit 3-by-3 matrix gives E[RA]=35/12-t/8, E[R]=19/16, E[A]=3/2, hence covariance 109/96-t/8. Three disjoint exchangeable largest-magnitude dominance events give t<=1/3, strict inequality from a positive-probability common narrow interval. Attainability t=0 and a separated-scale family t->1/3 are explicit; continuous mixture achieves intermediate t. Exact-rational sign/rank enumeration of five genuinely continuous scale laws independently checks 73 identity groups, including all cross moments. No extrapolation beyond n=3; symmetric atomless iid assumptions essential.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary record-age laws, renewal descriptions and multi-time record-count literature address universal record counts or ages, not the coupling to strict-positive occupation time. The present statement is a complete sharp distribution-dependent range already at three increments. All nine indicator cross-moments have been checked and the universality boundary does not follow from record or occupation marginals alone. Dedicated published-finding corpus and web searches did not retrieve an exact equivalent, though this does not establish worldwide bibliographic uniqueness; a nonobvious reduction of earlier occupation/ladder-variable identities remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An older exact fluctuation identity jointly generating occupation counts and record indicators may imply this 3-step case despite absent matching search terms.
Absence of an indexed match cannot establish worldwide first publication.
Uninspected portions of longer record literature may contain a related mixed moment.

value.rationale: Sparre Andersen universality makes both the record-number and positive-occupation marginals fundamental distribution-free observables. Their coupling is not determined by either universal law. This result locates the first nonuniversal dependence horizon, identifies a single natural triangle-dominance mechanism, and fully determines the sharp attainable interval including endpoint topology and explicit extremal families. The complete classification clarifies a concrete boundary to marginal universality, rather than measuring an arbitrary statistic or a routine substituted parameter.
